items.title: 24.3.2 Distinction between Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Amines

source_refs.note: Topic 24.3.2 with Quick Check 24.3, answered (PDF 123-124). The book's secondary-amine equation is drawn with a garbled 'NH-HNO2'; it is written correctly here. Answers need review.

blocks.text: Primary, secondary and tertiary aliphatic amines are distinguished by their reactions with nitrous acid (nitric(III) acid), HNO2. Nitrous acid is unstable, so it is made in the mixture from sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid: NaNO2 + HCl -> HNO2 + NaCl.

items: Primary amines form diazonium salts (diazotisation): CH3CH2NH2 + HNO2 + HCl -> CH3CH2N2+ Cl- + 2H2O. With nitrous acid, primary amines give off nitrogen gas, seen as bubbles.
Secondary amines form N-nitrosoamines, yellow oily liquids: CH3CH2NHCH3 + HNO2 -> CH3CH2N(CH3)-N=O + H2O (N-methyl-N-nitrosoethanamine).
Tertiary amines react to form a soluble nitrite salt, with no visible sign of reaction: CH3CH2N(CH3)2 + HNO2 -> [CH3CH2NH(CH3)2]+ NO2- (N,N-dimethylethanammonium nitrite).

blocks.alt: NaNO2 + HCl gives HNO2 + NaCl. Below: CH3-CH2-NH2 (ethanamine) + HNO2 + HCl gives CH3-CH2-N(+) triple bond N Cl- (ethane diazonium chloride) + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Ethanamine and nitrous acid give ethane diazonium chloride (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 123).

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-NH with CH3 on the N (N-methylethanamine) + HNO2, with NaNO2 + HCl over the arrow, gives CH3-CH2-N(CH3)-NO (N-methyl-N-nitrosoethanamine) + H2O.
blocks.caption: N-methylethanamine and nitrous acid give an N-nitrosoamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 124).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed equation reads 'NH - HNO2'; it is + HNO2, as drawn above. The label printed 'ethaneamine' is written ethanamine.

blocks.alt: CH3-CH2-N with two CH3 groups (N,N-dimethylethanamine) + HNO2 gives, in square brackets with a + charge, CH3-CH2-N(CH3)2-H, followed by NO2- (N,N-dimethylethanammonium nitrite, soluble).
blocks.caption: N,N-dimethylethanamine and nitrous acid give a soluble nitrite salt (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 124).
